item.title: Top Democrats call to rein in AI buildout after midterms sweep: 'National data center moratorium now'
item.description:
- Democrats’ big victory in the 2026 U.S. midterm elections has some of its top leaders calling for restrictions on data centers and the artificial intelligence build-out.
![US Senator Bernie Sanders, Independent of Vermont, speaks during the The Pro-Human Assembly, convening the leadership of nearly every constituency of the pro-human movement in the wake of the rise of artificial intelligence, in Washington, DC, September 15, 2026. The event is organized by the "Future of Life Institute," an advocacy group calling for human control of AI, avoiding concentration of power, and strong oversight. (Photo by SAUL LOEB / AFP via Getty Images)](https://image.cnbcfm.com/api/v1/image/108363195-1789494139297-gettyimages-2294931488-AFP_C8EA8N2.jpeg?v=1789494213&w=1858&h=1045&vtcrop=y)
Stocks linked to the artificial intelligence build-out declined slightly on Wednesday in the wake of the election, but the selling intensified [on Thursday](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/04/stock-market-today-live-updates.html) as investors worried Democratic wins could have a real impact on data center construction.

item.title: When Use of Artificial Intelligence Conflicts With Employees’ Sincerely Held Religious Beliefs (US)
item.description:
As businesses embrace generative artificial intelligence (AI) in the workplace, a new trend is emerging: conscientious objectors requesting exemption from AI tools to accommodate their sincerely held moral views.
The American Humanist Association (AHA) recently signed onto the [_Luxembourg Declaration on Artificial Intelligence and Human Values_](https://humanists.international/policy/luxembourg-declaration-on-artificial-intelligence-and-human-values/) and exhorted secular humanists to examine the economic, environmental, anti-creative, and anti-competitive impacts of AI.
New technology presents new challenges, and AI is no exception.

item.title: Workshop on artificial intelligence is today
item.description:
## **Workshop on artificial intelligence is today** A live interactive workshop on how artificial intelligence (AI) is transforming opportunity discovery across careers, research, entrepreneurship and innovation is at 5 p.m. today (Nov. 5) in the SIU Student Center Auditorium.
“The Future of Opportunity Discovery: An AI Founder Talk and Live Workshop” is presented by Johnbosco Nnamso, a doctoral student researcher in computer science and a research and teaching assistant in SIU Carbondale’s School of Computing. The workshop is from 5–6:30 p.m.
The presentation will examine how AI is changing the way emerging opportunities are recognized and turned into innovations that create real-world impact. Participants will take part in a live interactive opportunity discovery workshop.
Henry Hexmoor, professor of computer science and program director of SIU’s Artificial Intelligence+ program, will participate in the faculty perspectives and discussion session.
His research focuses on artificial intelligence, machine learning, intelligent embedded systems, and scalable software architectures.
